en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga,
Pācittiya Section
The Chapter on the Painted Hall 43.
The Training Rule on Weaving Thread.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were spinning thread.
People, while wandering on a tour of the monastery, saw them and complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs spin thread? They are just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures!"
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so forth]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six weave thread?"... [and so forth]...
“Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs are weaving thread?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, could the group-of-six bhikkhunīs spin thread?
This, monks, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: "Whatever bhikkhunī should spin thread, there is an offense of wrong-doing."* (*The full rule includes the penalty of confession.)
“Whatever nun should spin thread, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Regarding “whatever nun”: whichever such [nun]... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"A sutta" means:
There are six kinds of cloth:
linen, cotton, silk, wool, hemp, and jute.
"Kante" means...
If she herself spins it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) for the act;
for every winding and unwinding, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
There is no offense—
She weaves a spun thread,
she is insane,
she is a first-time offender.
The third training rule is concluded.
